chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Umar ibn Sahl ibn Isma'il al-Dinawari narrated to us. He said: Zayd ibn Isma'il al-Sa'igh narrated to us. He said: Mu'awiya ibn Hisham narrated to us from Sufyan, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Khalid ibn Riba'i. He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) entered Mecca for one of his needs,

and he found a Bedouin clinging to the curtains of the Ka'ba, saying: O Owner of the House! The House is Your house, and the guest is Your guest; and for every guest there is a gift from his host — so make my gift from You tonight forgiveness. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to his companions: Do you not hear the words of this Bedouin? They said: Yes. So he said: God is too generous to turn away His guest. He said: When the second night came, he found him clinging to that corner, saying: O Glorious One in Your glory! There is none more glorious than You in Your glory. Grant me glory through the glory of Your glory — a glory that no one knows how it is. I turn toward You, and I seek intercession with You by the right of Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad over You. Give me that which none but You can give, and turn away from me that which none but You can turn away. He said: So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to his companions: This, by God, is the Greatest Name in Syriac. My beloved, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings upon him and his family), informed me of it. He asked Him for Paradise, so He gave it to him, and he asked Him to avert the Fire, so He averted it from him. He said: When the third night came, he found him clinging to that corner, saying: O One who cannot be encompassed by any place, and from whom no place is empty, who existed without a 'how' —

— sustain this Bedouin with four thousand dirhams! He said: So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) proceeded to him and said: O Bedouin! You asked your Lord for hospitality and He gifted you; you asked Him for Paradise and He gave it to you; you asked Him to avert the Fire from you and He averted it. But on this night you ask Him for four thousand dirhams! The Bedouin said: Who are you? He said: I am 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. The Bedouin said: You, by God, are what I seek — with you I have laid down my need. He said: Ask, O Bedouin. He said: I want one thousand dirhams for a dowry, one thousand dirhams to pay off my debt, one thousand dirhams to buy a house, and one thousand dirhams to live from. He said: You have been fair, O Bedouin. When you leave Mecca, ask about my house in the city of the Messenger (may God bless him and his family). So the Bedouin remained in Mecca for a week, then went in search of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) to the city of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). He called out: Who will guide me to the house of the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali (peace be upon him)? So al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon them both) said from among the children: I will guide you to the house of the Commander of the Faithful, and I am his son al-Husayn ibn 'Ali. The Bedouin asked: Who is your father? He said: The Commander of the Faithful 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He asked: Who is your mother? He said: Fatima al-Zahra', the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds. He asked: Who is your grandfather? He said: The Messenger of God Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib.

He said: 'Who is your grandmother?' He said: 'Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid.' He said: 'Who is your brother?' He said: 'Abu Muhammad, al-Hasan ibn Ali.' He said: 'You have taken the world by both its ends! Go to the Commander of the Faithful and tell him that the Bedouin of the pledge in Mecca is at the door.' So al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) entered and said: 'O father, a Bedouin is at the door, claiming to be the one of the pledge in Mecca.' He (Ali) said: 'O Fatima, do you have anything for the Bedouin to eat?' She said: 'By Allah, no.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) dressed and went out, and said: 'Call Abu Abdullah Salman al-Farisi for me.' Salman al-Farisi (may Allah have mercy on him) came to him, and he said: 'O Abu Abdullah, offer the garden that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) planted for me to the merchants.' So Salman went to the market, offered the garden, and sold it for twelve thousand dirhams. He brought the money, and brought the Bedouin, and gave him four thousand and forty dirhams for his expenses. Word then spread to the beggars of Medina, and they gathered. A man from the Ansar went to Fatima (peace be upon her) and informed her of that, and she said: 'May Allah reward you for your errand.' Ali (peace be upon him) sat with the dirhams poured out before him until his companions gathered around him, and he took a handful at a time, giving one man at a time, until not a single dirham remained with him. When he came home, Fatima (peace be upon her) said to him: 'O cousin...'

...cousin, did you sell the garden that my father planted for you?' He said: 'Yes, for something better than it, immediate and deferred.' She said: 'Where is the price?' He said: 'I gave it to eyes I was too shy to humiliate with the humiliation of asking before they asked me.' Fatima said: 'I am hungry, and my two sons are hungry, and I do not doubt but that you are like us in hunger — not a dirham of it was for us!' And she took hold of the edge of Ali's (peace be upon him) garment. Ali said: 'O Fatima, release me.' She said: 'No, by Allah, or let my father judge between me and you.' So Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Muhammad, Allah sends you His greetings and says: Give my greetings to Ali and tell Fatima: it is not for you to strike against his hands nor to clutch at his garment.' When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came to the house of Ali (peace be upon him), he found Fatima clinging to Ali (peace be upon him). He said to her: 'O little daughter, why are you clinging to Ali?' She said: 'O father, he sold the garden you planted for him for twelve thousand dirhams and left not a single dirham for us to buy food with.' He said: 'O little daughter, Gabriel brings me the greetings from my Lord and says: Give greetings from your Lord to Ali, and I was commanded to tell you: it is not for you to strike against his hands.' Fatima (peace be upon her) said: 'I ask forgiveness of Allah, and I will never do so again.'

Fatima (peace be upon her) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) went to one side and my husband Ali to another side. It was not long before my father (peace be upon him and his family) came back with seven black Hijri dirhams.' He said: 'O Fatima, where is my cousin?' I said to him: 'He went out.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Here, take these dirhams, and when my cousin comes, tell him to buy food for you with them.' It was not long at all before Ali (peace be upon him) came and said: 'Has my cousin come back? For I sense a sweet fragrance.' She said: 'Yes, and he has given me something for you to buy us food with.' Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Give it to me.' She gave him seven black Hijri dirhams. He said: 'In the name of Allah, and praise be to Allah abundantly and purely; this is from the provision of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' Then he said: 'O Hasan, come with me.' They went to the market, and there was a man standing, saying: 'Who will loan to the Wealthy, the Fulfilling One?' Ali said: 'O son, will you give him?' He said: 'Yes indeed, by Allah, O father.' Ali (peace be upon him) gave him the dirhams. Al-Hasan said: 'O father, you gave him all the dirhams?' He said: 'Yes, O son. He who gives little is able to give much.' Ali (peace be upon him) then went to a man's door to borrow something from him. There he met a Bedouin who had a she-camel. He said: 'O Ali, buy this she-camel from me.' He said: 'I have nothing to pay for it.' He said: 'I will give you time to pay at the time of receiving.' He said: 'For how much, O Bedouin?' He said: 'For one hundred dirhams.'

Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hasan, take it.' So he took it. Ali (peace be upon him) went on and met another Bedouin, identical in appearance but wearing different clothes. He said: 'O Ali, will you sell the she-camel?' Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'What will you do with it?' He said: 'I will use it in battle in the first expedition your cousin wages.' He said: 'If you accept it, it is yours at no cost.' He said: 'I have the price with me, and I will buy it at its price — how much did you pay for it?' He said: 'One hundred dirhams.' The Bedouin said: 'Then you shall have one hundred and seventy dirhams.' Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Take the one hundred and seventy and hand over the she-camel: the one hundred goes to the Bedouin who sold us the she-camel, and the seventy for us to buy something with.' Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) took the dirhams and delivered the she-camel. Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'I went searching for the Bedouin who sold me the she-camel to pay him his price, and I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sitting in a place I had never seen him before or after — on the open road. When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) looked at me, he smiled with laughter until his back teeth showed.' Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah make you laugh and give you the good news of your day.' He said: 'O Abu al-Hasan, you are seeking the Bedouin who sold you the she-camel to pay him his price?' I said: 'Yes indeed, may my father and mother be your ransom.' He said: 'O Abu al-Hasan, the one who sold you the she-camel was Gabriel, and the one who bought it from you was Michael, and the she-camel was from among the she-camels of Paradise, and the dirhams were from the Lord of the Worlds, Mighty and Majestic. So spend them in good and do not fear poverty.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful — the title of Imam 'Ali ibn Abi Talib
key_terms.الِاسْمُ الْأَكْبَرُ: The Greatest Name — the supreme name of God that grants any supplication
key_terms.الْحَدِيقَةُ: The garden/walled orchard — planted by the Prophet (SAWW) for 'Ali
key_terms.الْمَلِيُّ الْوَفِيُّ: The wealthy and faithful — used to describe God as the One who repays generously
key_terms.قِرًى: Hospitality gift — the traditional gift given to a guest by a host
key_terms.نُوقُ الْجَنَّةِ: She-camels of Paradise — indicating the supernatural origin of the camel

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Imam Ali and the Bedouin at the Ka'ba in al-Amali of Shaykh Saduq?
ai.summary: This extensive narrative from al-Amali of Shaykh Saduq narrates a miraculous story centered on Imam 'Ali's (AS) extraordinary generosity and the divine approval it received. The hadith describes three nights of a Bedouin supplicating at the Ka'ba, 'Ali's (AS) recognition of the Bedouin's supplications as the Greatest Name in Syriac, 'Ali's (AS) selling of the Prophet's garden to fulfill the Bedouin's needs, giving away all the proceeds, and a confrontation with Fatima (AS) that was resolved by divine revelation through Gabriel. The climax reveals that the Bedouin who sold 'Ali a she-camel was Gabriel, the buyer was Michael, and the dirhams were from God — confirming that giving charity without fear of poverty is divinely rewarded.
